We say that additional evidence beyond the 14 municipalities, beyond the 112 named sites in the schedule E of the indictment is evidence that you can consider for that limited purpose but whether or not there was indeed a wide-spread or systematic attack and whether or not there was a campaign of terror directed against that population. I think I've covered all the points I wanted to make, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan, can I just ask a question which may be redundant, but I am not sure I fully understood the math in your intervention. You speak about the 14 municipalities yet schedule E of the indictment covers 17 municipalities. How did you reach the number of 14?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You'll notice that the schedule E, the last municipality has number 17 by it, but there are not 17 entries there. There are 13 entries. If you count the number of municipalities, there are 13. Despite the fact, the last one has number 17 beside it. That's the math, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. The municipalities had numbers assigned to them in other schedules, and so there is no allegation concerning, for example, Ilijas which is municipality number 12 in schedule F.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Sorry for not picking up on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: If I may respond very succinctly and briefly. The point about the scope of the report goes to the issue of notice which we received, and we received notice on several occasions previously, namely, the indictment paragraph 26 and 27 limit the scope of the charges to schedule E. On the 14th of August, the notice we received in relation to Riedlmayer specifically, I'm looking at it, refers to paragraph 26 and 27 of the indictment. The draft report we received on that same day, Riedlmayer says in his report at paragraph 13, I'm only considering schedule E and one municipality from F to make 14. So that's the notice we have. That's the position the Prosecution took, and that's why we are saying you should be limited in what you accept within the scope of that report. And the last thing, if it's correct that the evidence that Mr. Riedlmayer gives in relation to perpetrators is unreliable, then by parity of reasoning, secondary sources which can't be relied on for perpetrators should not be relied on for the dates during 1992. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm not sure I fully follow the logic of your last comment, Mr. O'Sullivan. Suppose a witness to whom Mr. Riedlmayer has spoken about who and when destroyed a particular mosque. If that witness would say, well, I have no idea who did it and then he may add, I think it was this or that armed group, but I'm sure that it happened on the 14th of August, for instance, wouldn't that be reliable evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The only person who could answer that question is the maker of the statement, not Mr. Riedlmayer. If you look at his report it doesn't go into any detail at all about that. And the Prosecution has conceded that they are not relying on his report about perpetrators. And we say well that's by the same reasoning because it's hearsay and unverifiable through confrontation by the accused, you should not be taking it on board in relation to whether or not it happened in 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, of course the information that we would get from a witness in the example that I mentioned would, of course, be hearsay evidence. But my point was that hearsay evidence may be admissible and may be given some weight. Right. I think that matter is covered. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I just wanted to follow up on that saying, this hearsay evidence about when a mosque was destroyed, for example, if the source of the information is a named individual, the individual happens to be the Imam, you may consider that fact as something going to his bias or motive for making a statement about when it occurred, but it certainly seems like he's a person placed in a position to know when it occurred, if that's his mosque, that's when he went every day to say prayers and do his business as an Imam, it's likely that he knows about that. And his motivation to lie about the date occurred seems to be something less suspect than perhaps his motivation to talk about who the perpetrators were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: As I understand, there's several matters raised by Mr. O'Sullivan and echoed by Mr. Pantelic. The -- well, as would have occurred in the course of what has passed between the bench and counsel, some of these matters such as the specific points of hearsay are going to have to be dealt with on an individual -- on a -- as they arise, but the broad objection which Mr. O'Sullivan first made to evidence of destruction outside of the municipalities named in the indictment, I think, is covered by the rule that we know as similar fact evidence and it is not excluded by the fact that it is not directly related to the municipalities named, but as Mr. Hannis has, in our view, correctly stated, are matters which the Trial Chamber is entitled to consider. And as I said, I think that's the only ruling we need to make at this stage. The other issues identified by counsel we will deal with as they arise. So if there's no further reason to delay the calling of the witness, would the usher please escort him to the stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Our next witness is Andras Riedlmayer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And welcome to the Tribunal. May I begin by asking you to read the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You may sit down. And may I begin by asking you to state your name and your date of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Andras Janos Riedlmayer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And your date of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My date of birth is November 28, 1947.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Mr. Riedlmayer, you have been called today to testify in the trial against Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin, and you have been called as an expert witness by the Prosecution in this trial. The Chamber has accepted your status as an expert and has also admitted or accepted your four reports as expert reports. Whether or not they will be admitted is a question that we will decide by the end of your testimony, but for the moment, you are called as an expert and will testify as an expert. This will imply that you will be able to provide your expert opinion on certain matters, but you are not obviously allowed to give evidence beyond your expertise, and in your case, your expertise, as the Chamber sees it, is limited to your observation of the destruction of mosques and other religious properties in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Defence teams in this trial have challenged your quality as an expert and have also challenged the solidness of your reports which is the reason why you have been called to testify. The Prosecution will be taking you through your reports in the span of two hours, after which the Defence for Mr. Stanisic will also have two hours for cross-examination and, finally, the Defence for Mr. Zupljanin will have three hours. So that makes altogether seven hours of testimony in this case. I know that you have testified before so you are well familiar with the proceedings. First it's the Prosecution for examination-in-chief and then it's the cross-examination by the Defence teams, and ultimately there may be questions from the Judges as well. I know that you are also familiar with the proceedings in the sense that we have to have a break every 90 minutes in order to change the tapes. Our next break will be in 20 minutes, and we expect that we will be able to finish your testimony by tomorrow then so that you can travel back to your home country. That's all I have to say except that I should add for reasons of principle that you know that there is -- you are supposed to tell the truth and that there is a severe penalty for providing false or incomplete information to the Trial Chamber. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Riedlmayer.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I would like to begin by showing you Exhibit 65 ter 10367.01. This is your curriculum vitae. Can you confirm for us that that is indeed your CV and that it's up to date?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: It is indeed my CV. And I believe it's a recent version, yes. Well, no, actually, it's an older version because the latest item mentioned is 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us any significant changes since this one was completed?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Quite a bit actually. I believe I submitted a copy of my CV for the Karadzic case, which I don't think this one is, but briefly put, I have continued to serve in a professional capacity at Harvard as an art documentation specialist and as director of the documentation centre for Islamic art and architecture. And also since 2001, as is laid out in my report, I have testified in a number of cases before this Tribunal that involved expertise in this matter both on destruction of cultural heritage in various municipalities in Bosnia and the same with respect to Kosovo. And I've had a number of publications also since 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. And we'll see if we can locate that more up-to-date one. You indicated in your report that you have previously testified in this Tribunal as an expert, and how many cases total before today, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, if you count the Kosovo testimony and the Bosnia testimony separately, it's twice in the Milosevic case, once in the Krajisnik case, once in the so-called Kosovo six case, Milutinovic et al., once in the Prosecutor versus Seselj, and once in the Djordjevic case, that was last summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next I'd like to show you 65 ter 10367.02. This is a report entitled "Destruction of Cultural Heritage in Bosnia-Herzegovina" and do you recognise that as a report you prepared specifically at the OTP's request for this case against Mr. Stanisic and Mr. Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did you bring a hard copy of that with you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I brought one, and I will ask the Court's permission to refer to it if I need to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Just a few things I wanted to ask you about in your report before I go to some of the specific site findings in your database. On page 7 of the English it's paragraph 14 regarding "survey goals and methodology." You do mention other reports that you prepared and which you wish to incorporate by reference because they cover many of the same municipalities that are a subject of this case?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And one of the -- some of the new sites that you visited specifically for this case were in the municipalities of Bileca, Gacko, Teslic, and Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: On the next page, paragraph 15, at the very end, you are talking about where you got information and photographs to put into your report. You mention some of those were from local religious communities and "from other sources considered to be reliable." Could you tell the Judges what those other sources you considered to be reliable were?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, these are actually laid out in a section of my report, but just to sum up, the other sources I considered to be reliable included the institutes for the protection of monuments, surveys carried out by a council of Europe survey team in the aftermath of the war, and photographs obtained from Tribunal investigators who took them on various missions to some of the municipalities. Wherever possible I sought to get multiple independent documentation for a given site in order to confirm my findings. Also I found that in cases where I visited a site and it was a sufficient time after the war that the site might have changed, it helped to obtain photographs taken at an earlier date after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next I have a question for you concerning paragraph 42, which begins on page 17 and actually on page 18. You mentioned some of the sites you went to where you discovered the mosque that had previously been there had been destroyed and in some cases levelled to the ground with the rubble removed. You mentioned that sometimes you were able to locate the former site in part because of an old lime tree, which is something traditionally planted next to a certain mosque. I had a question for you, first of all, about lime tree. Where I come from in Phoenix, Arizona I had a lime tree in the backyard which was the citrus fruit, but I think you explained to me, you mean something different here?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes. Lime tree is English is another name for Linden. In B/C/S it's Lipa, and it was traditionally even in pre-Christian times a sacred tree among the Slavs, and the custom involved in Bosnia of planting a Linden tree, a Lipa, next to the mosque, it was often referred to in poems and folk songs as [B/C/S spoken] Linden tree next to the mosque, and often when the mosque was gone, the ways one could trace that it had once stood there would be, first of all, to look for foundations or traces of rubble, but usually the tree would be there, and very often there would be remains of gravestones and sometimes also deposits of rubbish on the site, but thereafter its destruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: A few questions to follow up on that. By tradition or custom, was such a tree planted in a particular position vis-a-vis the mosque?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: It was usually to the right of the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you used the word Lipa. Is that the Bosnian?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: That's the Bosnian term.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How do you spell that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: L-i-p-a.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next is a typographical error I think you pointed out to me at the bottom of page 21? In the English, we have paragraph 56; at the top of the next page 22, we have paragraph 62. Could you explain that for us?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: There is no missing text. I was editing material, this is the technical section of the report on the use of the database, and I took out some text that was no longer relevant and forgot to readjust the numbering, but there is no material substance missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So there are no paragraphs 57 to 61, that's just a numbering --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: It's a numbering error.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. In your report you make a reference to at page 23 appendix 1, a description and assessment of documentation sources. You list a number of sources of material that you referred to to prepare your report in conjunction with your field survey information. I want to look at one of those separately now, which is 65 ter number 10367.07. This is a map that is referred to in your report at paragraph 89, which you indicate had been marked by Mr. Bekir Besic. Can you tell the Judges about what this map is?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: It's a large-scale map of Bosnia-Herzegovina on to, which Mr. Bekir Besic was a member of the council of the Islamic community of Banja Luka during the war and is now a refugee, marked the locations of destroyed mosques mainly based on the published documentation of the Islamic community of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which I discuss.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can we zoom in one more level, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you explain to us what the markings are, first of all. What are the green circles, if you know, and then what are the little red dots?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: The green circles indicate major towns such as Travnik, Zenica, Banja Luka, Bihac. Each of the small red circles indicates a mosque that was damaged or destroyed, and if you look very carefully right of centre, there are some light green squares, those are mosques that have survived intact. That is halfway between the twin green circles of Travnik and Zenica and the Bosnian border in the north, you can see some light green markings. Those are mosques that survived intact.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you personally do any investigating or checking of this document to see if the sites indicated as destroyed matched up with what knew from your own work?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: In my various surveys for the Tribunal, I have covered approximately the -- all or part of 35 municipalities of Bosnia and so I checked it against the sites that I had actually visited and found none there that were wrongly indicated. In addition, I had access to Mr. Omerdic's [phoen] book published by the Islamic community of Bosnia, which served as the base for this map, and again checked and it appears to be correct in all its references. I thought it was a useful graphic representation of the extent of damage and to the extent that it coincided with parts of Bosnia that I had documented, it appears to be fully reliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I propose to move to tender all the documents, I want to tender at the end of his examination and I'll wait to do that then.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you about one more before I think we reach time for a break. In paragraph 86 there's a reference to a supplementary survey database. Can you tell us what that was?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: When I was asked to prepare this report, I found that there were four municipalities that were to be included for which I had not previously prepared site reports, and so I was given a set of specifications by the OTP, and I prepared the report last summer. The database is based exactly on the same methodology and format as my previous reports for the Tribunal, but they cover these four additional municipalities. Some of them I had done field surveys in either formally or informally, and some of them I was able to acquire additional documentation from sources I judged to be reliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll take a look at some of those when we return.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have one more I can ask him about before the break, Your Honours, if that's all right. This is 65 ter 10367.06.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'll tell you, Mr. Riedlmayer, this is a document called "Statistical Addendum: Sacral Sites of the Non-Serb Communities in the Surveyed Municipalities Damaged or Destroyed in 1992."

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, I have it here. This is a statistical analysis that I performed for the purposes of the Krajisnik case, and I was asked to go through my database and simply separate out sites as to the date of destruction, and within that it speaks for itself. Now, the overlap of municipalities covered is not exactly the same as the one for this case, but substantially so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I see that there are some municipalities listed here that are not in our indictment, but we can do the map separately.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this would be a convenient time for me to break, if that's convenient with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. So we would return in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, just to advise you, what I intend to do is show the witness a series of some of the photographs from his database pertaining to some of the sites listed in the schedule, but I don't intend to show him pictures for all 112. I hope to show a representative sample and then we'll tender the databases pertaining to all those sites at the end unless there is an an objection or you prefer me to handle it in a different way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Welcome back, Mr. Riedlmayer. Before I resume by showing you some photographs from your database, I did want to quickly go back to your CV. I understand -- I see Mr. Pantelic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise to my friend. Okay. Now, it's okay. For the moment I was unable to make a connection with the LiveNote. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand we have the updated version of your CV. I'd just like to have you take a look at 10367.01 and see if indeed now I have the correct one in e-court.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, that seems correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to turn to Exhibit 65 ter 10367.10, and go to page 37, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, can you explain for us what this is? I know in your report you describe now these pages are put together, but now we have one in front of us. Could you walk us through it, please.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes. This is an entry from my survey database. The top rubric consists of the name of the building, in this case it's very easy because it doesn't have very many names. Some buildings are known by multiple names. So I have it in English and in B/C/S. I have the district, which is the municipality in Bosnia, the name of the town, GPS co-ordinates so you can locate it, the date of construction, the historical period, and various categories of what kind of building it is. Then there's the section on building condition. In this case, if you look at the photographs before and after, you can see that the building, in fact, was completely destroyed. The site was empty in the photograph taken at the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Right now we are seeing a pre-war photograph on the screen?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: What we are seeing on the screen is a photograph taken in 1985 and published in 2004 in a book published by the archdiocese of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In the photo on the left.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: And what you see on the left is the site of the destroyed church. Again it was published by the Roman Catholic archdiocese. The photograph was taken after the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could scroll down.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: There's some informant information.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This gives a date of destruction and the fact alleged that a church suffered damage and then subsequently the ruins were removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go I think to the bottom of the page or the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The source of your information this this particular case?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Is the book edited by father Franjo Maric. It's celebrates 300 the anniversary of the archbishop.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can we go to page 31 of this document. This is another site in the Teslic municipality.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Okay. This is in the village of Donji Ruzevic. It's a modern mosque. It was rebuilt from the ground up after an earthquake in 1987 and the picture of the mosque, which is the -- shows the mosque after the war in its destroyed state shows the stump of the mosque -- minaret where you can see that it basically is cut off at the base, and you can see hanging bits. This is very typical of minarets that have had some sort of internal blast. Modern minarets are held up with reinforced concrete, and the rebar, the iron bars that vertically hold up the structure gets forced apart from the explosion and typically dangles out in a rosette, and you can see bits of that on top. In front is the -- what remains of the foundations. In the rear is the Imam's house, which had been rebuilt after the war. In this case, the photograph comes from the journal of -- published by the Islamic community. If you scroll down you will see the source cited. The reason I had to resort to this photo is because the mosque since then has been rebuilt, and this was the one I found that showed clear evidence of -- that it had been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: When you went to locations where the mosque had been totally destroyed, how were you able to determine that you were at the right spot? There's no building there anymore. Can you tell the Judges what you did in that situation.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: All right. Well, in the best of cases, I had, first of all, pre-war photographs. Pre-war photographs are useful because they show features in the background, either natural features or other buildings, some of which may have survived after the war, and there are many examples in my survey where you can see that. Secondly, in most cases on my survey, I was guided to these spots by people who knew these locations. I usually engaged a clergyman who had in the pre-war period been familiar with the place, and the clergyman would accompany me for several hours or sometimes the whole day going from site to site, and so I placed some reliance on that. Also when you get to a site, unless the foundations have been dug up, and even that leaves a trace in the form of a depression, you can often tell differences in growth of vegetation. Even grass doesn't grow well on building rubble. It's very spotty, and in some cases you can actually see the complete outline of a foundation. Very often when buildings are destroyed and even the rubble removed, there will be fragments that remain at or close to the site, so there are all these various ways in which you can conclude that a building has been there even if it's not there anymore. And then, of course, there are things that I've already mentioned such as the Linden tree in the case of a mosque and very often the acts of desecration like big piles of smelly garbage placed on the site or graffiti written around it. So these are the various ways in which one can do that. But I would also say that in only some of the cases were the ruins completely removed. In most cases, as it this one, you can see elements of the mosque still remaining on site.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next I would like to show some photos from another one of the databases. This is Exhibit 10367.12. If we could start out by looking at page number 538. Just a minute, we are getting to the page. There we go.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Okay. This is a mosque in Kljuc municipality. It is one of those that goes by multiple names. Pudin Han-Velegici is the village it is in. It's complicated by the fact that Velegici, like many Bosnian villages has an uphill and a downhill part. This particular part of the village is next to the main highway between Kljuc and Sanski Most. It's also known at the mosque of Hadzici, Hadzici being the name of the immediate neighbourhood. It was a modern mosque built just a few years before the war, and it indeed was completely destroyed. At the time I visited the site, the mosque had just been rebuilt. The opening dedication had been held the previous day, but I could, first of all, tell that the mosque had been there because a small element of the old mosque had been left as a memorial next to the new mosque. One could also tell from the surrounding area, and I was fortunate enough in this case to have a number of photographs taken at various dates both during and after the war showing the destruction. So what you see here on the left is a photograph published by the British photojournalist Paul Harris, who was there in at the very beginning of 1993. You can see that the minaret in the back has been truncated, and the mosque itself has collapsed. What you see resting partially on the ground is the concrete slab of the roof. It originally had one large dome and then three small domes over the entrance. And there had been some sort of blast which blew out the walls and the roof just pancaked down on the ground. Then if you go down you can see two further photographs showing that, in fact, by the end of the war there had been additional destruction, and at the very end only one of the little domes over the entrance was the only element of the mosque that still existed. The rest was all the rubble. Can you page down one more, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we go one more page to page 540.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Can you scroll up. If you go back one more. Yes, here you go. So here you see the benefit of multiple sources. This was a photograph taken in 1997 by the council of Europe, and you can see the rubble and the sole remaining element. The photo on the right was the one I took, and the rebuilt Imam's house is in the back and the little dome is, can't see it well on this photo, but it's to the right of the rebuilt mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Before we leave this, I would indicate, Your Honours, in the indictment schedule E we have reference to Pudin Han mosque and then a semicolon Velegici mosque. Mr. Riedlmayer, are there two mosques in that area?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: No, there is only one. I believe that's an error in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And so the name is Pudin Han-Velegici mosque, meaning one building?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: One building, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could go next to page 583 in this exhibit in e-court. Now we are going to Kotor Varos. If we could scroll down. This is a Catholic church?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is the Catholic church in the town of Kotor Varos, and I visited this site in July of 2002. This is an interior view looking towards the alter. You can see the roof is missing, and there are signs of fire, which I noted, and if you scroll down slightly, you can see the same space although looking in the other direction towards where the other photograph is, so one is looking away from the alter at the bottom and the one on top is towards the alter. So you can see how badly destroyed the interior is. The exterior of the church was also damaged. It had two modernistic steeples which were collapsed. One of them collapsed on to the adjacent parsonage.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could go now to page 739. Again we are going to another municipality now. We'll have a look at Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is the exterior view. Okay. This is the Roman Catholic church in the town of Prijedor. I visited the site in 1992 by which time, of course, the church was no longer standing. I obtained photos of the destruction, some taken during the war and then some pre-war ones as well as my post war photo. The building that was still standing at the time of my visit is the one you see on the left of that photo, which is is the modern parish centre built next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page in e-court. On the right, that's a pre-war photo?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: On the right is the pre-war photo. The region had a bad earthquake in the 1960s, and the old steeple collapsed and they built a modern steeple next to it. The photo on the left is a photo taken during the war which shows the remains of the knave of the church as of late 1992. I believe the photo was taken by a German photojournalist and it was published in the book by Roy Gutman.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could look at page 745, another site in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is the mosque in the old town of Prijedor, Stari Grad. And this is an example of what I was talking about where you can see the foundations simply by the growth of vegetation. That is a corner of the building. The mosque itself was where that mobile home there is, and you can see a tall Muslim gravestone off to the left. If you look at pre-war photos, you can see a number of those lined up in front of the mosque, but basically the mosque is completely gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is that what you were talking about, the pre-war photo?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is it. And if you look near the corner of the building at right, you can see a very tall tombstone, which I believe may be the same as in the photo that I took in 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me show you next one from the Zvornik. This is at page 1132. 1132. Sorry, maybe I misnumbered. I need ERN 0557-5022, so it's a hundred pages farther on judging by the ERN. That's it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The Riejka mosque in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: The Riejka mosque in Zvornik was the main mosque in the centre of Zvornik. And what you see on top is a photograph I took in July of 1992. Here you see an example of the old Linden tree and the big overflowing trash container at the base of it, and I also have some pre-war photos in which you can see the same tree. The site for a number of years after the war had been turned into a parking-lot, but by the time I got there in 2002, court cases had been brought and at least they had to fence it in, but they still hadn't rebuilt it at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go to the very next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Dr. Riedlmayer, just to be sure that there's a correct replication of what you said, you said the photograph was taken in July of 1992 yet the photo that we just saw appeared to be from July 2002.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I meant 2002. If I said 1992, I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Good. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The very next page.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: These are two pre-war photos taken just before the outbreak of the war. You can see the tree and the mosque to the right of it, and this is a slightly different view taken from uphill, but you can see the mosque in the right centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: And if you look closely at the tree, you can see some match. The surviving tree still has a gap in it, the same as this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me go now to Brcko. It's page 292 of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the Sava mosque or [B/C/S spoken] or old mosque in Brcko. It's again in the centre of town. This street you see immediately to the right is the main street at Brcko market, and this top picture is the site as it appeared in the summer of 2002 when I was there. If you take a careful look at it, you can see that part of the site is depressed. I was told by the chief Imam of Brcko that not only was the rubble removed, but even the foundations had been excavated. If you look at the iron bridge at the right, you will see that in the pre-war photo as well, which is right below.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, if we can go to the next page in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can see the iron bridge and the light poles. I'm not sure the light poles are the identical ones, but I believe they are at the same spots, and this is the mosque as it was before it was blown up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And from other information you received, were you able to determine where some of the rubble from this particular mosque ended up?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, I found references by two forensic archaeologists who worked on a Tribunal sponsored exhumation at a mass grave-site on the outskirts of Brcko. One of them is Dr. Richard Wright whose testimony I cite, and the other one was Dr. Rebecca, I forget her last name, Simmons, Summers or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Saunders in the --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Saunders, yes. Rebecca Saunders, who is a forensic archaeologist from the US, and a -- I actually contacted Professor Saunders who had mentioned the mosque rubble in an interview she came and gave right after she came back from the exhumation, and she confirmed to me that yes indeed they had seen it. This is also what the local Islamic community had told me about. I did not go to the site, and I did not personally see any of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I believe you indicated that you referred to Dr. Richard Wright's testimony in the Ilicic [phoen] case?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, I believe, it's in a footnote to my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to go to another exhibit. I have four more sites and two more exhibits, Your Honours, then I think I will be nearly finished. This is Exhibit 10367.08. And I'm not sure about the page numbering in e-court. 1029.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is the older of the two mosques in the town of Visegrad, and it's variously known as the town mosque, the Gazafer [indiscernible] mosque or the market mosque. And its site right now is an empty triangular square with a couple of concrete park benches in the middle. If you take a very careful look at the post war photo I took and note particularly the building on the right and the lower building immediately to the left of that, you may be able to also see that in the pre-war photo that I have of the same site. You can see a taller building and then a lower garage-like building to the left of it behind the entrance columns of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think it's another pre-war photo of the same mosque.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is a photo taken in the other direction. The previous one was to the left as oriented from the post war photo. This was straight on in the same direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next if we could go to page 1035. I think five pages on from here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the Sarajevo mosque or emperor's mosque. It's the other mosque in Visegrad, it's at the opposite end of the main street, the Glavna Ulica in Visegrad. At the time I visited there what you see on top is all you could see. Again if you look very carefully, you can see traces of the outlines of the foundation. There's a corner right above the right-hand bottom corner of the picture, you can see the corner of the foundation. If you take a careful look at the buildings in the background, the apartment buildings, I believe they can also be spotted on the pre-war photo, similar pattern of windows. The entrance of the mosque faced the street, and these buildings were immediately to the right of it as you looked at the entrance, and it's yet another one of those cases where it was completely destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. This was also called Bikavac?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: It was also called the Bikavac mosque because it was next to the Bikavac neighbourhood in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And lastly to one more exhibit, 10367.11. If we could go, first of all, to page 1 of that one.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is the Roman Catholic church in the town of Bosanski Samac. The top picture was taken by an ICTY investigator right at the end of the war. What you see in the foreground behind the iron fence is the empty site where the Catholic church used to be. What you see in the right rear is the Serbian Orthodox church across the street which remained intact. Next picture shows the iron fence with the new church rising behind it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: And this was the local parish priest who was there supervising the reconstruction of the church, and he had both a pre-war photo and a model of the church that he showed for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could go now two pages on. Also in Bosanski Samac another site.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is the town mosque variously called as Azizia [phoen] mosque or mosque of Mir Ahmed it's in the very centre of Bosanski Samac. It's in a small park surrounded by the buildings of the town centre, and at the time I was there there was just the empty lot, the rubbish bin, and the tree. And if you scroll down you can see the mosque in the centre of the surrounding buildings. And if you go down one more page you can see --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Here you see two pre-war views of the mosque again with the tree next to it, next to the right side of the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see in your database entry this is referred to as the mosque of Mir Ahmed or the Azizia mosque?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is it also known as the town mosque?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, every mosque has a mosque near the centre of town and it's variously known as the town mosque, [indiscernible] or the market mosque, the [indiscernible] but many mosques such as this one also bear the names of the donor who originally found it or repaired the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was there any other mosque in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: No, there was only one mosque and one Catholic church.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. There is a few things I want to touch-up with you in terms of names and spellings. In our indictment schedule E for Donji Vakuf there's a reference to Pusak's three mosque. We have Prusak spelled P-r-u-s-a-k?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: It should be spelled with a C at the end. It's Prusac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you did find three mosques in --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I visited Prusac myself, and there were, indeed, three mosques there, and they are in the database submitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: As far as you know, no town or village in Donji Vakuf spelled P-r-u-s-a-k?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Similarly regarding Sanski Most, we have in our indictment a reference to the Restovo Karanovici [phoen] mosque, and I think you indicated to me that Karanovici should be Karani [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Karani. That's really a variant name. The Ovici just indicates that this is a settlement of the sons of, so it's just different ways of saying almost the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Two more, if I may. Doboj there's a preference to [Microphone not activated] and I think you indicated that should be P-r-i?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And lastly in Visegrad, reference to Drinska mosque with an A?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: The village is called Drinsko, and it's actually a very strange name for the village because it's not on the river, but it's spelled with an O.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Riedlmayer. I have no further questions for you at this time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I would like to tender his CV, his report, and the associated documents that we've talked about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, only the ones you covered today in the direct examination, the ones we talked about, you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I think I've talked about everything on the list at least briefly in terms of the exhibits from 10367.01 through .12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So all the documents on the list?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Can we wait until the end of cross-examination to make final submissions on that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The report that you prepared for this case incorporates, among others, the report you prepared for the Milosevic case; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And the Milosevic case report was prepared in 2002?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And the title of that report is, I'll just read it to you, "Destruction of Cultural Heritage in Bosnia and Herzegovina, 1992 to 1996, Post War Survey of Selected Municipalities." Correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Okay. And when you prepared that report for Milosevic, you were interested in covering the period from 1992 until the end of 1995 until Dayton?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: If I've understood what you said correctly, you -- your first step was to seek information to establish the state of a site pre-war?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: That actually happened at various stages in the process. Before I set out to Bosnia, I tried to get all published information that was available. That, as you might guess, would produce variable results. Famous sites the ones that are mentioned in the art books and the tourist books would have lots of photos, little village mosques or churches would not. Then throughout the time I was doing my field-work in Bosnia, I tried insofar as possible to collect photos from the local communities if they had any and in some cases they would show me photos and I would take photos of the photos. In some cases they would hand me little fundraising brochures that had pictures of the pre-war building. So this was a process that continued throughout.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So the upshot is you agree, you were trying to establish the state of the site pre-war?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Then when you went into the field in 2002, you would establish the state of the site as it existed after the war?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So your focus was that period from 1992 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The -- you looked at -- my friend the Prosecutor showed you the statistical addendum that you prepared for Krajisnik. That's 65 ter 10367.06. Is it your position that the information contained in this addendum, which indicates which sites were damaged or destroyed in 1992, is correct? Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Would you concede if there were examples in your supporting materials that, in fact, you record 1993 as the date of damage or destruction, if that were the case, would you accept that the information in this addendum is wrong?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Anything is possible. We are talking about close to 400 sites. I put this together during proofing at the last-minute request of the Prosecutor, just manually going through my survey. On the other hand, I would not suspect that there would be much variation.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: But you will accept if there are references to 1993, which you recorded, you would accept that and also accept that there may be mistakes in this document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: It is possible that it could be off by a very small percentage.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Right. For the record, we would refer in future reference to the Catholic church in Kljuc, Catholic church in Samac, the Gornja Kamenica mosque in Zvornik, the Karanovici mosque in Zvornik and [indiscernible] mosque in Zvornik. Now, with information that you recorded in your database concerning the alleged date of destruction, you never independently went out and investigated to see whether that information was accurate, did you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: That was not something -- first of all, I was not there during the war so I was not there to witness any of it. Insofar as possible, if there was information available from third sources such as, for example, a report by a journalist who passed by the site during the war and noted that the mosque was destroyed or was still standing, I would include that as corroboration, but I wasn't out there, you know, conducting a criminal investigation. I was there to take pictures of buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Okay. And you were not a military researcher, are you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I'm not a military specialist, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And you do not know when or whether there was any military action in any of the Stanisic/Zupljanin municipalities in 1992, do you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: No, I don't. However, I would say that I was able to make observations both of the buildings as they stood when I visited them, most in 2002, some at other dates, and looking at pictures of the buildings taken often during or immediately after the war, and so it was possible to see certain things. First of all, the context, were buildings around the mosque or church damaged; and secondly, the nature of the destruction itself. One would expect that a building that had been in a middle of at battle zone would have lots of bullet-holes, would have impact holes. It's -- although I'm not a military expert, as a result of these field investigations, I've conducted both in Bosnia and in Kosovo, I've seen hundreds of buildings that have suffered damage and have developed some expertise in judging how they were destroyed. But you are right, I wasn't there when they were destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Riedlmayer.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I know that you are born on 28th of November?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It seems that all good people are born on that. I'm also born on the 28th of November, almost ten years after you, but we are human building, Mr. Riedlmayer, we all made sometimes mistake, and you can say agree with me that even in this kind of work certain mistakes or errors could occur. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: [B/C/S spoken].

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I would like to bring to your attention the titles of your previous reports. For example, my learned friend Mr. O'Sullivan mentioned a report that you made -- that you prepared for Milosevic case in 2002, and the title is is "Destruction of Cultural Heritage in Bosnia-Herzegovina 1992, 1996, a Post War Survey of Selected Municipalities," excerpt by you. That's the correct title?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: That's the title it bears.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then in 2003 you filed a report for Krajisnik case; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then in 2009 you filed actually, if I'm not wrong, two reports, one for Karadzic case, the other for this particular case, Stanisic/Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I believe that the proper title should be -- I mean, in Milosevic case actually my opinion is that you actually use a more precise title. With regard to --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we have a question rather than lawyer's opinion. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, Mr. Riedlmayer, that actually a word of a known Serb cultural heritage is not appropriate word, that maybe just word Bosnian cultural heritage would be more appropriate? I mean, this prefix of non-Serb might give us certain confusion?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What was the reason --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: The reason it reflects the terms of reference for the mission. As I state in the reports, once you get beyond the title, the mission I was given, the terms of reference was to look at cultural heritage of the non-Serb communities, which, in effect, means the Bosnian Muslim, Bosnian Croat communities in the affected municipalities. I agree that if I were doing this for any other purpose, it is an awkward way to put it. But it simply reflects the way in which the mission was framed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you would agree with me, would you not, Mr. Riedlmayer, that no matter of ethnicity or ethnic background, all Bosnian heritage belongs to all three constitute nations in Bosnia; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: If you look at any of my articles and writings I argue that position consistently.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, so you also allow the possibility that certain members of Serb community actually followed or practice Muslim or Catholic religion; am I correct ?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: That gets into matters of self-definition.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, my --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I'm saying depends on when you are talking, to whom you are talking, these are not absolute terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. Mr. Riedlmayer, hold on, please. You allow the possibility that a number of citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina who are Serbian nationality and Serbian ethnic background might be a member of Muslim religion community or Catholic community, they are practicing. Do you allow that possibility, simply yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: It is a possibility, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So even for that particular number of Serbian citizens might be a very strange to have this kind of title if tomorrow someone will read it, would you agree with me? This particular specific non-Serb, that's my point. Would you agree with me to maybe amend your title in near future or --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: As I --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I object to the relevance of this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Another matter, Mr. Riedlmayer, I was reading your publications that you actually attached, a list of publication that you attached to, I believe it's, yeah, it's a part of your CV. And I don't see a particular -- particular publication which you published in 1993 under the title of a brief history of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It was a part of Bosnian manuscript in gathering project. Could you explain us why you didn't put this particular --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, I know what you are referring to. It was a website, and it was not a formal publication in the sense that it didn't go through a publishing house or an editor. It was done for an occasion. It has no footnotes. It is not a scholarly publication. It is similar in nature to a letter one might write to a newspaper or a pamphlet. My publications, such as they are, are for the most part things written for formal journals, books. They are different in nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you stand behind this particular publication that I mentioned?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: What do you mean stand behind? I did publish it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You are the author, you accept all that you wrote actually?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I wrote that in 1993 on the basis of the information I knew in 1993 or thought I knew. If I were to write the same thing again, I probably wouldn't. You know, all of us learn something over the course of nearly two decades. I would point out that a similar historical survey of the history of Bosnia-Herzegovina following roughly the same outline but in a formal fashion properly sourced and so forth, appeared in my publication "From The Ashes" which is also cited in my bibliography, and I would stand behind that one, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Riedlmayer, just one question, please. Actually, what exactly would you change -- but before that, please tell me, my understanding is that you were a sort of, I would say, misinformed or to some extent, poisoned by newspaper articles and at that time in 1993 and that because of lack of proper information, you actually wrote this paper, yes?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, first of all, the title was a brief history of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I believe printed out it runs through six pages A4. Of that, I think all but the last two pages dealt with remote history. The part that dealt with the war, dealt only with the first year of the war --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: And so I would say when I wrote this in 1993, the information available was what was available via the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And the media -- the media -- the media overexaggerated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, as I understand the witness's testimony, he has explained, bearing in mind that he is a scholar, he has explained that the 1993 article, which he accepted in terms of the question initially put, is no longer part of his list of publications, has been overtaken by further research and whatnot and the relevant parts are in the more recent work "From The Ashes," I think is the name of it. So I am not sure what is the point of exploring the quality of this work which he has, for all practical purposes, perhaps abandoned is too strong a word but from the witness's own testimony has been overtaken by further research and further knowledge bearing in mind, as I said, that he is a scholar. So where are we going?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, I was checking certain transcripts from a case in Seselj. It's page 7454, where, in fact, Judge Antonetti asked Mr. Riedlmayer about his position with regard to his previous work, and all this line was related to his credibility. Mr. Riedlmayer now gave us a very detailed and precise answer with that regard, and what I'm just want to ask him is whether he actually stays now with certain words in his work or not. And I will make -- I will make the quotation of that. Simply as that. It goes to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, well, move directly to the particular quotation from the earlier work that you seek to challenge him on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Riedlmayer, are you staying today with your -- with the part of your work that I just mentioned, and I will quote: "The nationalists have also enacted" meaning Serb nationalists, "the nationalists have also enacted anti-masogenation statutes that make it a crime for a non-Serb to marry or engage in sexual relations with a Serb." Are you staying with this position today?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: No, I believe that was mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. And then are you staying with the other portion of your work that in the zones under Serb control actually the non-Serbs were required to display white flags on their places of residence, do you stay by that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: In part. In the fact that I believe there has been testimony before this Tribunal that in certain locations people did have to display white flags.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When we are here at the same topic, where actually -- which cases you are following here within the Tribunal? Did you follow this particular case?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Not as much as some of the preceding ones, but feel free to remind me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: More or less, you are following the cases?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, insofar as they are covered from the outside. I don't sit in or read the transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And tell me, you were -- you were called as an expert witness before the ICJ and you were expert on behalf of government of Bosnia-Herzegovina; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And actually, you were hired, sort of say, by whom? By government of Bosnia-Herzegovina or particular counsel to whom you were in preparation of that case?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: By the deputy agent for Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Van Den Biesen. He engaged me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And he paid you actually.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, I got an honourarium.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would Mr. Pantelic be so kind to speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, you are asked to speak into the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And while reviewing this particular transcript, our learned friend Ms. Joanna Korner was examining you at that point, yes?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And tell me in preparation of that testimony, did you speak with her and discuss cases before the Tribunal which --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: No. At that time she wasn't working for the Tribunal. It was actually the first time I met her. And my only discussion with her prior to my testimony I had a prepared text, and we indicated the points where she would ask the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And, Mr. Riedlmayer, correct me if I'm wrong, but I think that the part of your testimony before the ICJ actually was related to the sort of historical practice that Muslim mosques were built on the, let's say, historical foundations of Serbian Orthodox church; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: That wouldn't be how I would put it. Could you rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Actually, correct me if I'm wrong, but the part of your testimony was -- is realisation that in history the Muslim religious buildings such as mosques were built on the foundation of a former Orthodox church which was destroyed during the history?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I don't recall that being part of my testimony, but you could refresh my memory. As a matter of fact, as came out in cross-examination, for example, in the Seselj case, my position is that this was extremely uncommon. In a few cases in Kosovo, not Bosnia, there were churches that were converted into mosque or mosques built on the ruins of a church. In Bosnia this was extremely uncommon. It happened only in a few places, one famous one is in Jacija where a Catholic church was turned into a mosque and then in the subsequent centuries it got ruined in an earthquake and it's still there as a ruin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What about Bijeljina case?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't see on the list of exhibits that Mr. Pantelic was going to use with this witness any ICJ transcript. So if he is going to confront him with what he said in the ICJ transcript we should have a page reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, we are just --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... foundation was with regard to the practice in history, so tell me --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The question was confronting him with something he allegedly said in his ICJ testimony, and your rules of procedure require a counsel doing that to make a specific page reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Riedlmayer, are you aware of such practice in Bijeljina in particular?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I am aware.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That's not moving on. That's continuing. That's not moving on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Judge Delvoie has not switched on his microphone on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Moving on, as I understand it, is go to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Riedlmayer, actually, you in your CV mentioned that that you were between 1969 when you graduated and until 1972 you were a freelance interpreter; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You were basically travelling around Middle East Turkey, that region?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Okay, the freelance interpreter is a different category. Basically what I did is in graduate school after I finished my masters degree, I got a fulbright fellowship, and I went to Turkey to do research in archives and manuscript libraries, and while I was there I was making money in order to pay groceries by translating.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And tell me, later on you went to Iran to have certain additional, I think, education, language education, historical education?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, I took a summer course in Persian at the university of Tehran.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, during your career, I'm also speaking about the Bosnia, your work within Bosnia, tell me, did you ever been approached by any of foreign intelligence services like AID in Bosnia or Iranian intelligence services or Turkish during your work? Do you have any context like that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And you consider yourself as a non-biased and objective expert in the field of heritage of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And you in your work did not check in collection of materials, you did not check any particular additional document within the archive of Republika Srpska, so your work was only focused on the archive of so-called Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I did not do archival research, I did field research. Insofar as I relied on local sources, it was for photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You did not contact any of government officials of Republika Srpska like ministry of interior or Ministry of Justice or anything like that? You don't have any particular contact with these officials, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So you actually made your report only on the basis of sources from Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Muslim Croat; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, no, if you look at the municipalities, most of my field-work actually happened in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But sorry --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: And most of the information I got was not from government authorities but from the local religious communities who were the owners of these buildings and had documentation concerning. I will take --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: -- one thing back about that. I did obtain from Republika Srpska municipal archives, cadastral records for many of the mosques and churches that were destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Riedlmayer, you didn't interview any, let's say, potential informant of Serb nationality; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: You mean within the Republika Srpska government?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And as you said, you are not military expert, you are not sort of art expert, you are librarian and bibliographer; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I am an art documentation specialist. That's what I've done for the last 25 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but you are not an --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Not an archaeologist.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In narrow sense an art expert like someone who can evaluate the art as itself or make some records, you are bibliographer and librarian basically?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, if you are asking can I, you know, date a Rembrandt or something like that, no, that is not my specialty. However, I, as far as documenting buildings, most of what one does in that case is, in fact, relying on the work of scholars who have done that. Yes, I know how to document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Tell me, in fact, you do not exactly how and when certain mosques and Catholic churches were destroyed within Republika Srpska; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: What is the question again?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The question is, do you have personal knowledge of how and when number of religious objects, buildings that you cited were destroyed actually?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I have no firsthand knowledge, no. I have seen documentation of various sorts but I have no firsthand knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So you actually know only, sort of say, of you have knowledge of consequences, but you don't know the way -- when, how, by whom it was done, you don't know that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, I have collected things like television video footage taken of mosques being destroyed as in Banja Luka, Bijeljina. I have collected photographs, dated photographs that show a building immediately during the process of destruction so in that sense I have documentation, but no, I was not present when these things happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And speaking of Banja Luka, actually I don't see any particular religious object that you mentioned because all it was done beyond the time-frame of this indictment because this indictment is only related to the end of 31st December of 1992? Actually in Banja Luka if something was done it was after December of 1992; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, if you look at the title of my report, Banja Luka is not among the municipalities that I was asked to cover for this particular trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Riedlmayer, I don't have any further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The live application to admit the documents that have been tendered is now granted, and the documents are admitted and assigned an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit P1395 through P1406, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And, Mr. Riedlmayer, we thank you for your assistance to the Tribunal, and you are now released as a witness, and we wish you a safe journey to home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So it's that time when we take the adjournment for the day; do I gather?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Do I gather --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour. We have no other witnesses available for this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Is there any other matter that we need deal with -- that we need assemble tomorrow with which to deal? So we take the adjournment to Monday morning at 9.00 in this courtroom. I wish everybody a safe weekend. Thank you.
